title: Basic credentials with an empty password
summary: A synthetic Basic token whose decoded user-pass is a user-id followed by a colon and nothing else.
rationale: A token with an empty password has the credential shape but may hold no confidential portion; the scheme neither permits nor forbids it. The user-id alone is not shown to be secret, so the expectation is not settled by the sources.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, ADR 0019 item 7 (#114), empty password): expect it to be unflagged. The decoded text is a user-id and a colon with nothing after it: no confidential part. Weak evidence: RFC 7617 has no explicit wording on an empty password. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history.

sources.supports: the first colon in a user-pass string separates user-id and password from one another; text after the first colon is part of the password

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Maintainer-only (ADR 0020): decided by the sole maintainer, not reviewed, not independent validation; queued for retro-review (#154). Authored from the cited standards read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. All values are synthetic and were not tested against any service. Header coalescing, parser and action policy, decoded-token mapping and product masking stay with the downstream repositories.
